question.problem:
What is the sum of the series $1-\frac{{(5\pi /3)}^{2}}{2!}+\frac{{(5\pi /3)}^{4}}{4!}-⋯+\frac{(-1)^{n}\,(5\pi /3)^{2n}}{(2n)!}+⋯\,?$

The sum of the series is
{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
We recognize that the series looks similar to the Maclaurin expansion for $f(x)=\operatorname{cos}⁡x:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡x=1-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2!}+\frac{{x}^{4}}{4!}-⋯+\frac{(-1)^{n}\,{x}^{2n}}{(2n)!}+⋯\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $x=\frac{5\pi }{3}$ into our Maclaurin expansion gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{5\pi }{3}) & =1-\frac{{(5\pi /3)}^{2}}{2!}+\frac{{(5\pi /3)}^{4}}{4!}-⋯+\frac{(-1)^{n}\,(5\pi /3)^{2n}}{(2n)!}+⋯ \\ \frac{1}{2} & =1-\frac{{(5\pi /3)}^{2}}{2!}+\frac{{(5\pi /3)}^{4}}{4!}-⋯+\frac{(-1)^{n}\,(5\pi /3)^{2n}}{(2n)!}+⋯\,.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the sum of the series is $\frac{1}{2}.$
